entry_state: Lease surrender, pension changes, opening production and funding restrictions require separate histories. Restoration cash classification depends on the payment activity. Corporate-asset impairment uses already adjusted units, and partial-goodwill tests distinguish notional amounts from recognised losses. Revalued impairment and the origin of tax remain to be developed.
exit_state: Impairment and tax preserve the origin of each equity effect. New information reallocates remaining depreciation; an old error instead corrects prior profit and opening equity without creating cash. Publication and ingestion cutoffs select report editions separately from the discovery date. The comparative-report discussion continues beyond the earliest opening balance.
findings: Revalued impairment reconciles the net asset decrease 37.5 to OCI loss 30 and profit loss 7.5; the reversal and rate-change examples retain the respective origins.

The estimate branch allocates remaining 97.5 over 45 months; the error branch retains the original six-year life and corrects prior profit. These are different facts, not elective treatments of identical evidence.
The correction separates prior equity, current-quarter depreciation and report presentation. The comparative equity bridge reaches 267.5 without repeating the opening correction.
Publication and system-entry cutoffs are explicit; an earliest opening balance does not supply an entire restated prior income statement. No new confirmed defect.
